doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Technology, synthesizers and small amps
summary: Pallo prefers guitar to synthesizers and lightens his gear with small amps and Bucky's Jazz Cat.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Are you at all into music technology as far as gadgets and computers and all that kind of thing?

No. I see them in the musician’s magazine when I get it every month they’ll show something that you should get, it’s either a drum machine or something for something to do with electronics and I just look at it and say okay, I really don’t need it. I tried when synthesizers first came out on guitar I tried that and it was great, you can get the string sound behind you and also the chord changes at the same time, and I said to myself you know I’m a guitar player. I’m going to go back to playing guitar. And the synthesizer is © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-
sitting in the back room now, I have five or six of them, they just sit back there, I just don’t use them anymore. I’d rather play guitar.
Right. And plus all of a sudden you find yourself going to a gig and you’ve got all this gear.
Oh the stuff to carry. I know. And that’s what I’m trying to eliminate. You’re trying to carry small things.
Yeah, the older you get the smaller your gear becomes.

That’s right. That’s correct. And I love the gigs like two weeks ago a fellow said, “Just bring an acoustic guitar.” And I said wow, I haven’t had this in a long time, not even an amp, just an acoustic guitar. Oh that was great. And then there are some where I just bring a small amp and I bring that little, the smallest amp I have.
I love Bucky’s, he’s got this little —
The Jazz Cat. Or which one?

Oh he’s got — well have you seen the new one? He’s got the Jazz Cat now. I have one of those too. It’s only 23 pounds, it’s a new one, and that’s light too and I’ll carry that around too. As long as you get the sound that you want. If you’re going to play with a big five, six pieces, then it’s hard to use a small amp. It’s very hard. And I use Bucky on some of my jobs where it’s just myself, Bucky and Jerry Bruno. I guess you’ve heard of Jerry, he plays bass. And we do a few things and I’ll use my Epiphone and he uses his guitar, and very small amps we use. Great sound.
